strongest_counterclaim: The (pullback_v_is_dry, current_vs_ibd_candidate_pct) regime is not a real mechanism but a proxy artifact driven by two confounders: (a) pullback_v_is_dry is inferred from NULL vs non-NULL pullback fields, where NULL almost certainly means 'no recent corrective base detected by the screener' (not 'volume contracted during a basing') — so the flag is really tagging 'had a tagged base at all,' which is tautologically correlated with B0 selection; (b) current_vs_ibd_candidate_pct's median delta between winners and false_negatives is only -0.29 (std delta -0.20), the WEAKEST signal in the numeric_contrasts table, while mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20, up_day_ratio_20, and px_vs_ma50 all carry larger standardized deltas (-0.85 to -1.19). The proposed 1.5–2.5 'sweet spot' is a band the data cannot statistically pin and is bracketed by the very false_negatives it claims to explain (false_negative_median = 1.69 sits inside the band). The apparent regime is a re-labeling of the existing B0 selection logic plus a momentum proxy, dressed up as a structural insight.

attacks.issue: pullback_v_is_dry is not a measurement — it is a missingness pattern. NULL pullback_duration_weeks / pullback_pct in the case JSON (entity_ead73f4390, entity_4fdc3699fd, entity_3472243e0c, entity_84824e6a20, entity_b6bcccdf6a, entity_40ea0cfb3b, entity_ad2bfdee3f, entity_05b4c6b1f7, entity_bec51a4227, etc.) means the screener did not flag a corrective base, not that volume was 'dry.' The researcher is conflating 'no base detected' with 'volume contracted during a base' — these are opposite regimes (momentum extension vs. basing). The 8 false_positive_ruin cases with NULL pullbacks are then being used to argue for a 'dry pullback' filter that would do nothing to them, because they never had a pullback to begin with.
attacks.why_it_matters: If the variable the regime is conditioned on does not measure what the mechanism claims, the entire causal story collapses. The dry-pullback filter cannot filter the no-pullback cases, so the ruin cluster it claims to address is structurally outside its reach.

attacks.issue: Snapshot contamination destroys the effective sample size. snap_71486ed83c contributes at least 6 cases (entity_df5478102d, entity_d8e8e7b814, entity_535a1beed7, entity_bfb308b24a, entity_2c58cebc59, entity_3472243e0c, entity_de1c657364) and snap_d0d57b1e40 contributes at least 5 (entity_6618d3e80c, entity_ad2bfdee3f, entity_bec51a4227, entity_05b4c6b1f7, entity_84824e6a20). Same date, same market regime, same sector correlations — these are not 27 independent observations, more like ~8 effective independent market contexts. The 1.5–2.5 band is fitted on roughly a handful of dates.
attacks.why_it_matters: With effective n ≈ 8, the 'sweet spot' band is a single-cluster artifact. Any band chosen post-hoc on this sample will look meaningful on the same sample but has no held-out validation. The researcher explicitly claims underpowering but then treats the band as actionable.

attacks.issue: The false_negative_median current_vs_ibd_candidate_pct = 1.69 falls INSIDE the proposed 1.5–2.5 sweet spot. The regime would therefore KEEP the false negatives it is supposed to exclude, while its claimed remedy (raising the lower bound to exclude unresolved basing) contradicts the data: the unresolved bases that eventually worked have x ≈ 1.69, not x < 1.5.
attacks.why_it_matters: The band is internally inconsistent — the lower bound 1.5 is below the false-negative cluster median, so the regime cannot be the mechanism that separates winners from false_negatives on this feature. Either the band should be set lower (which would admit the false_negatives it targets) or the feature is not doing the work the researcher claims.

attacks.issue: Confounding with mom_20 and vol_ratio_5_20 is unaddressed. The standardized deltas rank: up_day_ratio_20 (-1.19), vol_ratio_5_20 (-1.05), mom_20 (-1.00), px_vs_ma50 (-0.85). The proposed regime uses only current_vs_ibd_candidate_pct (std delta -0.20, the second-weakest in the table). The 'dry pullback' label correlates with NULL pullback fields, which in turn correlates with high momentum/extension states (high ma10_slope_5, high px_vs_ma50). The regime is likely a redundant encoding of the same momentum cluster already captured by mom_20 and vol_ratio_5_20.
attacks.why_it_matters: If the regime is just a momentum proxy, encoding it as a separate two-axis score adds complexity without incremental information. The marginal value over a simple mom_20 + vol_ratio_5_20 filter is unproven and probably near zero.

attacks.issue: Pullback_pct direction contradicts the 'shallow dry-up = winner' narrative. Numeric contrast shows false_negative_median pullback_pct = -7.3% vs selected_winner_median = -15.9%. Winners have DEEPER pullbacks, not shallower. The prior role's claim that 'dry short bases (3–5 weeks)' are the regime treats depth and duration independently, but the data shows winners pull back harder on average.
attacks.why_it_matters: If winners have deeper, longer pullbacks (e.g., entity_3adc078f01: -42.3% over 9 weeks, entity_2c58cebc59: -25.1% over 6 weeks), then a filter preferring short shallow basing is filtering against the actual winner signature, not with it. The 'dry-up' frame is a storytelling overlay on a number that points the other way.

attacks.issue: Entity_6618d3e80c is a clean falsification of the upper-bound argument. It carries the dual label false_positive_ruin|selected_winner, with px_vs_ma50 = 0.337 (implying current_vs_ibd_candidate_pct is high, likely >2.5), yet it is also a selected_winner with large_win bucket. Any hard cutoff at 2.5 would drop a documented large winner. The regime cannot be a hard exclusion — the prior role acknowledges this — but then its predictive value reduces to a confidence weight, which is exactly what mom_20 and up_day_ratio_20 already are.
attacks.why_it_matters: A regime that must be implemented as a soft weight (not a hard cut) is indistinguishable from the existing continuous features. The 'piecewise' framing is not adding a decision boundary, just a reparametrization.

attacks.issue: base_duration_weeks (std delta -0.42) and base_mbox_count (std delta +0.34) are stronger and more direct measures of basing quality than the proposed pullback_v_is_dry proxy, and they are NOT in the regime. The mechanism claim ('supply exhaustion via volume contraction') would be more cleanly tested by these, but they are absent from the policy recommendation.
attacks.why_it_matters: The proposed regime ignores the variables that directly measure what it claims to measure, and substitutes a missingness pattern. If the policy is adopted without incorporating base_duration_weeks / base_mbox_count, the encoding is leaving signal on the table.

attacks.issue: Discovery-train-only fitting with no held-out forward validation. The labels (false_negative_relative, false_positive_ruin, etc.) were generated on the same 27 cases used to derive the regime. There is no out-of-sample evidence that the 1.5–2.5 band generalizes. The falsifiable_predictions the prior role lists are forward tests on a snapshot that has not been run.
attacks.why_it_matters: All regime boundaries cited (1.3, 1.5, 2.5, 3.0) are in-sample estimates with no confidence intervals. Acting on them as policy without forward validation is data dredging.

counterexamples_to_seek: A B0-eligible candidate from a DIFFERENT date cluster than snap_71486ed83c / snap_d0d57b1e40 with current_vs_ibd_candidate_pct in [1.5, 2.5], pullback fields NULL, that ends in ruin — would show the regime fails outside snapshot-71486ed83c.

A B0-eligible candidate with pullback_v_is_dry=True (i.e., non-NULL pullback fields), pullback_pct < -25%, pullback_duration_weeks ≥ 6, current_vs_ibd_candidate_pct > 2.5, that is a large winner — entity_2c58cebc59 and entity_3adc078f01 approximate this; need to confirm the regime's upper bound does not flag them as 'late momentum chase' when they were structurally sound.

A B0-eligible candidate with current_vs_ibd_candidate_pct = 1.69 (the false_negative median) that is a large winner — entity_535a1beed7 and entity_de1c657364 fit this; they directly test whether the proposed lower bound 1.5 is too high.

A candidate with high mom_20 (>0.20) AND high vol_ratio_5_20 (>1.5) AND current_vs_ibd_candidate_pct > 3.0 that is a selected_winner — entity_b00579f203 (mom_20=0.23, vol_ratio=1.58, px_vs_ma50=0.23) is one; tests whether the regime over-excludes high-momentum winners.

A B0 candidate where pullback_duration_weeks is short (3) but pullback_pct is deep (<-15%) — does not exist in the 27 cases but would test the orthogonality of duration and depth, which the regime implicitly assumes.
what_would_change_my_mind: Held-out forward testing on a snapshot NOT in this 27-case discovery sample, where the 1.5–2.5 band shows a statistically significant ruin-rate reduction (p<0.05, n ≥ 50) versus a control using mom_20 + vol_ratio_5_20 alone. Without this, the regime is unfalsified speculation.

A direct measurement of pullback_v_is_dry (e.g., volume during the drawdown window vs. trailing 50-day average) showing it is NOT equivalent to 'pullback fields non-NULL' — and that the measured version separates winners from ruin at a higher standardized delta than mom_20.

A demonstration that adding (pullback_v_is_dry, current_vs_ibd_candidate_pct) to a logistic/gradient model with mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20, up_day_ratio_20, px_vs_ma50 already in it produces a significant AUC lift (ΔAUC ≥ 0.03) on out-of-sample data. If not, the regime is redundant.

Evidence that the regime's two boundaries (1.5 and 2.5) are stable across market regimes (e.g., 2022 bear vs. 2023 recovery) and not artifacts of the particular date clusters that dominate this sample.

Replacing the NULL-proxy for pullback_v_is_dry with a directly measured volume-during-base variable that shows entity_6618d3e80c-style extended winners and entity_df5478102d-style shallow-pullback eventual winners being correctly separated — i.e., the mechanism works when the proxy is replaced with the real thing.
